alternativeDerivation: At an intersection the shared x-coordinate satisfies 0<x≤1 and 1/(1+x²)=√((1-x)/x). Both sides are nonnegative, so squaring is equivalent on this interval. Multiplying by the positive x(1+x²)² yields x=(1-x)(1+x²)², or x⁵−x⁴+2x³−2x²+2x−1=0. Polynomial division using the cubic supplied in the question gives (x³+x−1)(x²−x+1)=0. The second factor is (x−1/2)²+3/4>0 for real x; therefore the supplied cubic must vanish. The algebraic identity and positivity hold for all real x, and the domain condition makes the squaring valid. This proof does not assume the intersection is on y=x.
